arguments.gap: I need literature evidence on alternatives to bilinear interpolation for 2D real-valued learnable lookup tables (LUTs) with a fixed uniform grid of trainable scalar parameters. The baseline is: input (x,y) in [-1,1]^2, output real scalar, fixed uniform 16x16 grid = 256 trainable real parameters. Candidate total trainable real parameters must not exceed 256. I want to understand what interpolation/interpolation-free schemes (e.g., bicubic, Catmull-Rom, radial basis / scattered interpolation, higher-order splines, tensor-product basis, local polynomial fits, or grid-free parameterizations) improve expressiveness for locally high-curvature or non-uniformly-sampled functions, and what their parameter counts, boundary handling, initialization, and differentiability/training properties are. Please read actual method pages of at least 2 papers and report paper_finding vs transfer_idea vs limitations distinctly. Selection criteria: papers that give concrete interpolation formulas, parameter counts, and training/differentiability details for learnable 2D scalar maps.
arguments.success_criteria: Return a verified research_report.v1 covering at least 2 distinct publications whose method pages were actually read, each with: exact title+URL, the paper's own finding (not your inference), a concrete transferable interpolation/parameterization idea with its parameter count and differentiability, and stated limitations for migrating to a 256-parameter 2D real LUT. Distinguish paper_finding from transfer_idea and limitations.
